title: Cold-start mitigation controller for cross-region cutover
creator: Maya R. Patel
description: Implement a controller that minimizes cold-start cost and latency during cross-region cutover events by combining proactive KV-cache seeding, model-variant prefetch schedules, and short-lived shadow traffic with probabilistic routing hooks. Scope: controller service + runtime integration + console rollout controls + observability. Goal is to ensure cross-region handoffs meet latency SLOs (p50 < target) within N seconds of cutover without requiring full pre-warm of entire model fleet. Constraints: must work with Dedicated pools and Hosted autoscaled nodes, respect capacity quotas, and avoid panic-level cost spikes.
acceptance_criteria: Controller deploys as a k8s operator and registers with routing service
On simulated region outage, candidate standby becomes primary within configured quiesce window with <10% p50 latency regression compared to steady-state
KV cache seeding reduces first-request token median by >=40% on cold model variants
Traffic-prefetch scheduler respects capacity budget and never schedules more than configured buffer percentage
Console shows per-route readiness score and allows manual abort/accelerate of cutover
Integration tests (stage) pass: end-to-end cutover, rollback, and partial-capacity scenarios

decisions: Use probabilistic shadowing (0.5-2%) instead of full traffic mirroring to avoid double-cost and client-side duplication
KV cache seeding will be prefix-based and prioritized by historical token-frequency heatmap
Hand-off quorum requires 3 readiness signals: model health, cache-seed coverage >= X%, and observed p50 on shadow traffic below threshold
Rollback trigger: >15% increase in error-rate OR sustained p95 latency bump above configured SLO for 2 consecutive minutes
